national: Members of the eight parliaments mentioned an Auditor-General {{mentions}} times over the 12 months, in {{turns}} contributions to {{debates}} debates. Tasmania, Victoria and Western Australia account for about {{top3}}% of mentions, partly because of long set-piece debates. October 2026 was the busiest month, led by South Australia's committee examination of its Auditor-General's Report.

About half of all contributions used audit findings to argue a case. A fifth were procedural, such as tabling reports or committees considering them. About one in eight concerned the office itself: its powers, funding, independence or appointment, with independence and funding raised in the NT, WA, Tasmania and Victoria. About 5% sought or discussed a new audit or referral, most often in WA, where members pressed ministers over section 82 notices on withheld information.

The largest threads differed by parliament: TT-Line's solvency in Tasmania, the Suburban Rail Loop and road maintenance in Victoria, section 82 notices and the office's independence in WA, the North Adelaide Golf Course and major project costs in South Australia, regional roads and rail fleet procurement in NSW, the Brisbane games and ecotourism in Queensland, public housing and referrals in the ACT, and the office's independence in the NT.
